title: MODIS-Aqua Monthly Rrs - OC-SMART AC
description: The MODIS-Aqua Monthly Remote Sensing Reflectance (Rrs, unit sr-1) provides 8 spectral bands temporal resolution of one month and spatial resolution of 1 km over the Brazil oceanic waters and open ocean South Atlantic waters. This collection captures 7 visible, and 1 infrared channels using Level-1A images acquired from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) instrument onboard the NASA's Aqua satellite. The Level-1A data were processed into Level-1B and GEO using the Data Processing Tools (modis_L1B) from SeaWiFS Data Analysis System (SeaDAS) software. The Level-1B and GEO data were applied in the atmospheric correction OC-SMART (Fan et al., 2021) by the National Institute for Space Research (INPE, Brazil) and the Laboratoire d'Océanologie et de Géosciences (LOG, France) generating the Level-2 data. The Level-2 data has been mosaicked to generate daily maps capturing the complete Brazilian ocean waters. The daily mosaic data were reprojected to geographical (lat/lon) coordinates using as reference the European Space Agency (ESA) Ocean Colour - Climate Change Initiative (OC-CCI) into Level-3 grid. Both, the mosaic and the reprojection were done using the Sentinel Application Platform (SNAP) on its version 10. Finally, the daily reprojected data were temporal merged to create the monthly Rrs products using the geometric mean.
producing_org_raw: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA); National Institute for Space Research (INPE); Laboratoire d'Océanologie et de Géosciences

title: GL1.2 Model - Downward Surface Solar Radiation (Daily Mean)
description: Downward shortwave radiation flux (DSWRF) at the surface represents the solar energy incident on the Earth's surface. Various terms for this variable are found in the literature, including global solar radiation descending to the surface, where the term 'global' refers to total solar radiation, including direct radiation (arriving in line of sight from the solar disk) and diffuse radiation (solar radiation scattered by gases, clouds, and aerosols). Another term associated with its physical unit (W/m²) is global solar irradiance. The data are generated from instantaneous outputs inferred by GL1.2 model and visible channel images from GOES satellites (GOES-10, GOES-12, GOES-13, GOES-16, GOES-19). For each day, the instantaneous images are integrated using the trapezoidal rule, and the final value is divided by 24 hours to represent the daily mean irradiance (W/m²). Each daily data file is an image covering South America and the surrounding oceans. Each pixel in the image indicates the daily mean solar radiation. References: [G-STAR/INPE - Grupo de Radiação Solar, Terrestre e Atmosférica](https://satelite.cptec.inpe.br/gstar/GSTAR_principal.html); [GL1.2 Model](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2003JD003531).

title: MYD13Q1 v061 - Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF
description: The Aqua Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Vegetation Indices (MYD13Q1) Version 6.1 data are generated every 16 days at 250 meter (m) spatial resolution as a Level 3 product. The MYD13Q1 product provides two primary vegetation layers. The first is the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) which is referred to as the continuity index to the existing National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration-Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (NOAA-AVHRR) derived NDVI. The second vegetation layer is the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), which has improved sensitivity over high biomass regions. The algorithm chooses the best available pixel value from all the acquisitions from the 16 day period. The criteria used is low clouds, low view angle, and the highest NDVI/EVI value.

title: TOPODATA - Banco de Dados Geomorfométricos do Brasil
description: The TOPODATA dataset provides a Brazilian collection of geomorphometric variables derived from SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission) data. title: MODIS-Aqua monthly biogeochemical products
description: The biogeochemical products (Chlorophyll-a, Suspended Particulate Matter, Particulate Organic Carbon, absorption by Colored Dissolved Organic Matter, and Dissolved Organic Carbon) are derived from remote sensing reflectance (Rrs, measured in sr⁻¹) retrieved from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) onboard NASA's Aqua satellite (MODIS-Aqua) and atmospherically corrected using the Ocean Color - Simultaneous Marine and Aerosol Retrieval Tool (OC-SMART) (Fan et al., 2021). These products are generated from daily Rrs observations with a nominal spatial resolution of 1 km at nadir. For each day, multiple MODIS-Aqua swath tiles covering the study area are processed individually to produce the corresponding Rrs. The resulting Rrs tiles are then merged into a single seamless daily mosaic using the SNAP Mosaicking Tool, producing a daily Rrs composite that combines all available observations for that day. The daily Rrs composites are subsequently used as input for the retrieval of the following biogeochemical products: • Chlorophyll-a concentration (CHL, mg·m⁻³): estimated using the Combination Of Neural Network models in Estimating Chlorophyll-a over Turbid and Clear Waters (CONNECT) algorithm (Tran et al., 2025). • Suspended Particulate Matter concentration (SPM, g·m⁻³): estimated using a blend of two SPM algorithms (Salah Salah et al., 2025). • Particulate Organic Carbon (POC, mg·m⁻³): estimated by combining the algorithms proposed by Loisel et al. (2002, 2018), Tran et al. (2016), and Le et al. (2016). • Absorption by Colored Dissolved Organic Matter (aCDOM, m⁻¹): estimated from the remote sensing reflectance band centered at 443 nm using the algorithm developed by Bonelli et al. (2021). • Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC, µmol·L⁻¹): estimated using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) machine-learning approach (Bonelli et al., 2022). The monthly biogeochemical products are subsequently generated by calculating the geometric mean of the corresponding daily biogeochemical products on a pixel-by-pixel basis over each calendar month, producing monthly composites for each biogeochemical variable.

title: GOES-13/Imager - Level-3 - VIS/IR Imagery (Binary)
description: GOES-13 is a satellite of the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) series operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Launched on May 24, 2006, it is designed to monitor weather conditions in North America, South America, and the Atlantic Ocean region. It operates in a geostationary orbit, meaning it remains fixed relative to Earth, continuously monitoring a specific region of the planet. In 2017, it was replaced by GOES-16 (GOES-East) as the primary operational weather satellite for the United States. Since then, it has been placed in a backup position. GOES-13/Imager instrument captures 1 visible and 4 infrared channels at resolutions of 1km (VIS) and 4km (IR). The collection captures product files into individual STAC Items for each observation from the GOES-13 satellite. It contains binary files in a grid format for each of the 5 spectral bands. The files are encoded using int16 and represent a matrix of values (reflectance for VIS and brightness temperature for IR) with 1714 lines and 1870 columns. Note: The values must be read as a one-dimensional array and then converted in memory to a two-dimensional m x n matrix. These versions are generated by INPE using the process of mapping data from the original geostationary projection to a uniform space-time geographic grid (EPSG:4326) with 0.04 degrees spatial resolution. The geographical area used in the remapping process was chosen because it covers and highlights Brazil, South and Central America. The image reprojection operation is performed using the gdalwarp utility (https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html) with the nearest neighbor resampling strategy defined.

The Level-2 data has been mosaicked to generate daily maps capturing the complete Brazilian ocean waters. The daily mosaic data were reprojected to geographical (lat/lon) coordinates using the European Space Agency (ESA) Ocean Colour - Climate Change Initiative (OC-CCI) as a reference, then aggregated into a Level-3 grid. Both, the mosaic and the reprojection were done using the Sentinel Application Platform (SNAP).

title: SAMeT - Hourly South American Mapping of Temperature
description: South American Mapping of Temperature (SAMeT) is a newly developed product and operationally available for South America through the National Institute for Space Research (CPTEC / INPE) Weather Forecast and Climate Studies website. This product combines the observed data with the ERA5 reanalysis, making a correction of the temperature field using an estimated lapse rate. The Lapse Rate was estimated for four regions located over South America, and for the four seasons of the year. The estimated values for the Lapse Rate were, in all situations, lower than the standard Lapse Rate (-6.5 °C·km-¹). The combination of reanalysis and observations, together with the correction of the Lapse Rate produced more accurate temperature fields than those provided by ERA5, especially in regions with more accentuated topography.

title: Albédo de surface Sentinel-2
description: La méthode de calcul de l’albédo haute résolution (HR) Sentinel-2 (S2)  a déjà été utilisée dans le cadre du programme Copernicus Global  Land Service (http://land.copernicus.eu/global/) en considérant les données  PROBA-V (Roujean et al., RSE, 2018, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2018.05.015).  Elle utilise ici en entrée les données MAJA L2A et comprend deux étapes.  En premier lieu, un jeu de données spectrales est constitué par accumulation  de scènes S2 au cours du temps afin de disposer de mesures directionnelles  permettant d’inverser un modèle de la Fonction de Distribution de la  Réflectance Bidirectionnelle (FDRB). Du fait du champ de vue réduit de S2,  la directionalité provient surtout de la variabilité de la géométrie solaire,  et ainsi la qualité du produit albédo HR peut varier selon la longueur de la  période de temps choisie. En second lieu, un modèle de FDRB est inversé sur  chaque jeu de données directionnelles spectrales multitemporel pour servir à  simuler ensuite la réflectance dans toutes les directions. L’intégration du  modèle de FDRB sur l’espace des directions de visée fournit la réflectance  directionnelle hémisphérique (DHR en anglais) et l’intégration de l’albédo  DHR sur l’espace des directions d’illumination fournit la réflectance  bidirectionnelle hémisphérique (BHR en anglais). Il s’agit ici d’un produit  albédo DHR correspondant au midi solaire local. Il est fourni avec une  incertitude qui traduit l’erreur cumulée dans sa réalisation. La dernière  étape consiste à convertir les albédos spectraux de S2 en un albédo solaire.  La loi de conversion est obtenue à partir de simulations d’un modèle de  transfert radiatif incluant des milliers de couverts végétaux. Ce travail a  été réalisé dans le cadre du programme SCO (Space Climate Observatory) du CNES  au travers du projet sat4BDNB mené en collaboration entre le CESBIO et le CSTB  (Centre Scientifique et Technique du Bâtiment) et qui s’appuie sur la Base de  Données Nationales du Bâtiment (BDNB). La période choisie est du 1er juin au  30 septembre 2022. Un albédo HR moyen est généré sur cette période pour toute  la métropole selon un tuilage et une projection géographique calqués sur le  produit MAJA L2A. Le produit a été vérifié par inter-comparaison avec des  mesures faites à partir d’albédomètres positionnés sur 6 prairies françaises  équiréparties sur le territoire national. Les résultats statistiques donnent un  biais de -0.01 et une erreur quadratique moyenne de 0.02 en unité de réflectance.  La valeur de l'albédo a été multipliée par un facteur 10000 pour archivage.

title: Monthly and yearly synthesis of Water Surface occurence
description: SURFWATER data collection contains yearly and monthly water occurrence  maps (ratio of water detections over clear satellite observations during  a year/month period) on a 10m resolution grid. Such maps are extracted  from optical (Sentinel-2 L2 from MAJA) and radar (Sentinel-1 GRD  processed by S1Tiling) datasets. Supervised algorithms guided by the  Global Surface Water reference are used to classify water/land scenes  for each optical/radar observation. Based on MERIT DEM information,  Height Above Neirest Drainage maps (HAND) are used to remove false  positives. Based on the validation scheme on [Pena Luque, 2021],  single-observation water maps have a median F1 score of 0.89  (precision= 0.9, recall : 0.9) evaluated on 26 labeled scenes. This  dataset is a demo production for France metropolitan territory on 2019.  THEIA/hydroweb.next plans to produce daily SURFWATER maps along 2022. [Pena Luque, 2021] https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/13/16/3279,  Validatin dataset https://zenodo.org/record/4657020

title: CDS THEIA-MTD Sentinel Soil Moisture products (S2MP) over french agricultural plot
description: "The soil moisture maps were carried out at a plot scale using french RPG (declared agricultural plot register).  A map is provided each 6 days (12 days with Sentinel-1A and 12 days with Sentinel-1B). Inversion algorithm for estimating  soil moisture was applied for agricultural areas with any vegetation cover. Land cover map is used to  extract the agricultural areas. Sentinel-2 images corrected for atmospheric effects are used  to calculate the NDVI (Normalized Differential Vegetation Index). Using several in situ measurements  of soil moisture, the accuracy on soil moisture estimation was evaluated to be about 5 vol.%.  In the provided soil moisture maps (WGS84, EPSG: 4326), the soil moisture values (mv) are multiplied by 5.  In order to derive the estimated soil moisture value from the provided maps it is necessary to divide by 5 :  volumetric soil moisture (in vol.%) = value obtatiend from the map / 5. Null values in the soil moisture  maps = no data (no soil moisture estimation). The difference between this collection and the historical collection  labeled "S2MP:v1" lies in the standardization of input and output data based on the MGRS grid. Additionally, this  collection focuses exclusively on mainland France."

title: SUFOSAT (suivi des forêts par satellite): Submonthly Assessment of Temperate Forest Clear-Cuts in Mainland France
description: La carte des coupes rases en France métropolitaine, générée à l'aide des données radar Sentinel-1 par une méthode de détection de changement radar, fournit une information en temps quasi réel des zones de coupe rase avec une résolution de 10 mètres par pixel et une unité minimale de cartographie de 0,1 hectare. La carte permet de détecter les coupes rases avec une précision de 99,4% et un rappel de 80,9%, validée par rapport à 967 parcelles de référence. Cette carte accessible à tous offre des informations détaillées sur la dynamique des coupes rases dans les forêts tempérées françaises. Les coupes rases montrent une variabilité régionale significative et une concentration notable dans les forêts privées, qui présentent sept fois plus de coupes rases que les forêts publiques bien qu’elles ne soient que trois fois plus grandes.

title: Thermocity Land Surface Temperature
description: ASTER and ECOSTRESS thermal data are reprocessed to provide  a state-of-the-art thermal data set over 5 french metropolises :  Marseille, Montpellier, Paris, Strasbourg and Toulouse.  For each metropolises, a 100km square ROI is used. The dataset extends  from 2003 to 2019 for ASTER and from 2018 to 2020 for ECOSTRESS.  For each mission and each ROI, we generally provide at least one acquisition  during day and night, and during winter and summer.  All the data have been geometrically corrected to fit  Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission geolocalization. They are provided  in the original spatial resolution (70m for ECOSTRESS and 90m for ASTER),  together with and enhanced resolution for ASTER when synchroneous visible data  are available (30m). Atmospheric corrections have been refined  for ASTER thanks to original atmospheric profiles from Meteo-France.  Finally, a dedicated TES algorithm trained on urban materials is used  to derive land surface temperature and emissivity.
